summary: Fred Pfeil worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at Amherst College (~1967–1971), held a post at Oregon State University, and taught Ellison Banks Findly.

Frederick William Thomas was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at King Edward's School (~1877–1885) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1885–1889). He served at the India Office Library, UCL, Epigraphia Indica, Balliol College, and Oxford as Boden Professor of Sanskrit (1927–1937).

Frederik David Kan Bosch worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as chef of the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (~1916–1936) and held posts at Utrecht University (1938–1945) and Leiden University (1946–1957).

Fredrik Barth studied at the University of Chicago (~1946–1949) and Cambridge (~1953–1957) under Edmund Leach. He taught Rinzin Thargyal and held posts at Bergen, Oslo, Harvard, Emory, and Boston University.

Friederike Assandri works in Sinology and religious studies. She studied under Gunther-Dietz Sontheimer and Alexander L. Mayer, earning her PhD at Heidelberg University (~1997–2002), where she later held a post (~2017–2020).

Friedhelm Hardy specialized in Indology and religious studies. He taught Steven Collins and held academic posts at King's College London (~1975–2004) and the University of Oxford as Wilde Lecturer in Comparative Religion (1985–1987).

Friedrich Alexander Bischoff worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Paris (~1952–1959), taught William H. Nienhauser, Jr., and was Professor of Sinology at the University of Hamburg (~1982–1993).

Friedrich August Rosen was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp (~1824–1826). He held posts at the University of London, UCL, the Oriental Translation Fund, and the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

Friedrich Bechtel was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen (~1873–1876) under Theodor Benfey and August Fick. He held academic posts at Göttingen (~1878–1895) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1895–1924).

Friedrich Bollensen worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen (~1827–1831) and under Heinrich Ewald (~1830–1833), later holding posts at Gatchina Orphanage, Saint Petersburg State University, the Main Pedagogical Institute, and Kazan Federal University (1852–1856).

Friedrich Haag was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Zurich, Göttingen, and Berlin, including under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler. He held posts as Dozent at Zurich (1873–1884) and professor of classical philology at the University of Bern (~1878–1914).

Friedrich Hirth specialized in Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Leipzig University (~1864–1865), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1865–1867), and the University of Greifswald (~1867–1869), and later held a post at Columbia University (~1902–1917).

Friedrich Max Müller was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Paris under Brockhaus, Bopp, Burnouf, and Wilson. He held long-term posts at Oxford (1850–1900) and the Institut de France.

Friedrich Müller worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Theresianum, Vienna, and Göttingen, learning under Anton Boller. After posts at Vienna University Library and the Austrian National Library, he became professor at the University of Vienna in 1869.

Friedrich Rückert worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, and under Franz Bopp, and held professorships at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (1826) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1841–1849).

Friedrich Schlegel worked in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Göttingen, Leipzig, and Paris under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy, holding posts at Jena (~1800–1801), Cologne (~1804–1808), and TU Dresden.

Friedrich Weller specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied under August Conrady (~1910–1915), taught Manfred Taube, and was appointed Ordinarius for Indology at Leipzig University in 1928.

Friedrich Wilhelm is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who taught Renate Syed. He held posts at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1959–1964) and as professor at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1969–1997).

Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph von Schelling was a philosopher who studied at Bebenhausen, Tübingen, and Leipzig. He held professorships at Jena, Würzburg, Erlangen-Nuremberg, Munich, and Berlin, and taught Friedrich Max Müller.

Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl was a scholar of linguistics and other fields who studied at Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg. He held professorial posts at Halle-Wittenberg, Breslau, Bonn (~1839–1865), and Leipzig (~1865–1875).
